framework: AWS Security Best Practices + HackTricks Cloud AWS
description: Compute posture checks for ECS/EKS/EC2/Lambda attack surface, persistence, and credential abuse indicators

items.title: EventBridge rules trigger ECS tasks on a schedule (persistence indicator)
items.description: Scheduled ECS tasks can be used to maintain persistence or execute unauthorized workloads.
items.remediation: Review EventBridge rules/targets; restrict who can create/update rules and RunTask; monitor for unexpected scheduled executions.

pci_dss.reason: Monitoring scheduled execution changes reduces persistence dwell time.

items.title: ECS task definitions show drift / unexpected containers
items.description: Unexpected containers or task definition changes can indicate backdoored workloads.
items.remediation: Enforce IaC and immutable deployments; restrict RegisterTaskDefinition/UpdateService; review diffs and approvals.

pci_dss.reason: Change control helps prevent unauthorized modifications to workloads.

items.title: ECS workloads lack centralized logging
items.description: Missing logs reduce detection and incident response capabilities.
items.remediation: Enable CloudWatch Logs for ECS tasks/services and enforce logging in task definition baselines.

pci_dss.reason: Logging supports detection of suspicious activity.

items.title: ECS task roles or execution roles appear overly permissive
items.description: Excessive IAM rights assigned to workloads amplify impact of initial access.
items.remediation: Apply least privilege to task roles; use permission boundaries and scope resource ARNs.

pci_dss.reason: Least privilege reduces blast radius of workload compromise.

items.title: ECS task definitions contain plaintext credentials in environment variables
items.description: Hardcoded secrets in ECS environment variables expose credentials to anyone with DescribeTaskDefinition permissions and violate PCI DSS secrets management requirements.
items.remediation: Remove plaintext secrets from task definition environment variables. Use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store with secretOptions/valueFrom references instead.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorization.
All individual non-consumer user IDs and authentication factors must be managed via a secrets management solution.

items.title: EKS cluster endpoint is public without strong restrictions
items.description: Public EKS endpoints expand attack surface and increase likelihood of credential brute/abuse paths.
items.remediation: Disable public endpoint access or restrict CIDRs; enforce private endpoint where possible and use strong auth controls.

pci_dss.reason: Limit inbound access to system components to only authorized sources.

items.title: EKS control-plane logging is not fully enabled
items.description: Missing EKS logging reduces detection for authentication and API misuse.
items.remediation: Enable EKS control plane logs (api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler) and ship to centralized SIEM.

pci_dss.reason: Audit logs provide visibility into administrative access and security events.

items.title: EC2 instances with IMDSv1 and instance profile attached
items.description: Instances allowing IMDSv1 while exposing IAM role credentials via instance profiles increase SSRF-to-credential-theft risk.
items.remediation: Require IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=require), review SSRF exposure paths, and minimize privileges in instance profile roles.

pci_dss.reason: Hardening compute metadata access reduces known abuse vectors for credential theft.

items.title: EC2 user-data contains credential or remote bootstrap risk patterns
items.description: User-data scripts containing secrets or uncontrolled remote script execution increase post-exploitation persistence and lateral movement risk.
items.remediation: Remove embedded secrets, avoid unpinned remote script execution, and move bootstrap secrets to managed secret services.

pci_dss.reason: Secure deployment and configuration practices must prevent credential leakage in bootstrap artifacts.

items.title: Lambda function URLs exposed without authentication
items.description: Lambda Function URLs with AuthType=NONE create unauthenticated invocation paths from internet.
items.remediation: Set Function URL AuthType to AWS_IAM or place function behind API Gateway with robust authN/authZ controls.

pci_dss.reason: Access to system components must require unique identity and authentication.

items.title: Lambda execution roles appear over-privileged
items.description: Broad permissions in Lambda execution roles amplify impact of code compromise and enable lateral movement.
items.remediation: Apply least privilege to Lambda execution roles and restrict wildcard/resource-agnostic permissions.

pci_dss.reason: Execution identities must be constrained to business-required privileges only.

notes: Compute skill is scoped to ECS/EKS in the selected region. Evidence must remain passive (no active exploitation).
